descriptionChirho: Active transitive breaking or shattering of a physical object (bone, yoke, vessel, gate, idol), the basic Qal sense corresponding to Arabic kasara and Korean 부수다/꺾다.
Passive or middle-voice sense of being broken, becoming shattered, or suffering destruction, corresponding to Arabic inkasara/tahattama and Swahili passive -vunjwa/-vunjika.
Intensive or iterative breaking, smashing into pieces or thoroughly destroying, corresponding to Arabic kassara (Form II intensive) and Korean 부수다 with intensifying particles.
Adjectival use of the Niphal participle describing a state of brokenness, often applied to the heart or spirit (lev nishbar), corresponding to Arabic munkasir and Korean 상한.
Causative sense of bringing to the point of breaking open, used specifically for causing birth or breaking forth, corresponding to Arabic uftih.u (to open) and Korean 해산하게 하다.
Causative passive sense of being shattered or wounded from an external cause, expressing deep personal brokenness or injury, corresponding to Arabic inkasartu and Korean 상하였다.

Metaphorical extension of the Qal meaning to break or quench thirst, a specialized semantic domain distinct from physical breaking, confirmed by Hindi बुझाते हैं and Swahili zinakata kiu (quench thirst).
Extended Qal sense of crushing or oppressing persons rather than objects, corresponding to Arabic li-yash.aqa (to crush) and Korean 부수려고, implying destruction of people or power.
